blocks.text: And the philosophical meaning is the same one we’ve encountered from the very beginning.
blocks.directed: And the philosophical meaning is the same one we’ve encountered from the very beginning.

blocks.text: The guru, the disciple, the Goddess and the entire manifestation are ultimately non-different from Parameśvara.
blocks.directed: The guru, the disciple, the Goddess and the entire manifestation are ultimately non-different from Parameśvara.

blocks.text: The guru’s body becomes a culminating ritual support for that recognition.
blocks.directed: The guru’s body becomes a culminating ritual support for that recognition.

blocks.text: And then comes the final phrase.
blocks.directed: And then comes the final phrase.

गुरुशरीरे सप्तमः कुलयागः सर्वोत्तमः सोऽपि प्राग्यागसाहित्येन सकृदेव कृतः सर्वं पूरयतीति शिवम्॥
Guruśarīre saptamaḥ kulayāgaḥ sarvottamaḥ so’pi prāgyāgasāhityena sakṛd eva kṛtaḥ sarvaṃ pūrayatīti śivam.

blocks.text: And what are the final words?

28. The end of the Tantrasāra — the whole bloody thing was Śiva
And now.
blocks.directed:
28. The end of the Tantrasāra — the whole bloody thing was Śiva
And now.

blocks.text: Then the apparent limitation of the individual.
blocks.directed: Then the apparent limitation of the individual.

blocks.text: And the way the one consciousness can appear as innumerable limited beings.
blocks.directed: And the way the one consciousness can appear as innumerable limited beings.

blocks.text: Then we discussed the methods of recognition.
blocks.directed: Then we discussed the methods of recognition.

blocks.text: And the various forms of divine immersion.
blocks.directed: And the various forms of divine immersion.

blocks.text: The purification of the cosmic pathways.
blocks.directed: The purification of the cosmic pathways.

blocks.text: The continuing conduct of initiated practitioners.
blocks.directed: The continuing conduct of initiated practitioners.

blocks.text: And the authority of the scriptures.
blocks.directed: And the authority of the scriptures.

blocks.text: And finally, here in Chapter Twenty-Two, we reach the Kaula sacrifice.
blocks.directed: And finally, here in Chapter Twenty-Two, we reach the Kaula sacrifice.

blocks.text: A progressive movement through increasingly interior forms of worship.
blocks.directed: A progressive movement through increasingly interior forms of worship.

blocks.text: And what was the supreme teaching?
blocks.directed: And what was the supreme teaching?

blocks.text: That the divine reality isn’t confined to any particular manifestation.
blocks.directed: That the divine reality isn’t confined to any particular manifestation.

blocks.text: Not merely the absence of bliss.
blocks.directed: Not merely the absence of bliss.

blocks.text: Not merely withdrawal from the world.
blocks.directed: Not merely withdrawal from the world.

blocks.text: But the unrestricted consciousness that is the reality of both.
blocks.directed: But the unrestricted consciousness that is the reality of both.

blocks.text: And now we can finally understand why Abhinavagupta insisted upon the Kaula character of the ritual.
blocks.directed: And now we can finally understand why Abhinavagupta insisted upon the Kaula character of the ritual.

blocks.text: Because the whole point is the conscious integration of what appears differentiated.
blocks.directed: Because the whole point is the conscious integration of what appears differentiated.

blocks.text: And the awareness through which everything becomes manifest.
blocks.directed: And the awareness through which everything becomes manifest.

blocks.text: Nothing independent remains outside the ultimate reality.
blocks.directed: Nothing independent remains outside the ultimate reality.

blocks.text: The highest sacrifice doesn’t require sacrificing consciousness to attain something beyond it.
blocks.directed: The highest sacrifice doesn’t require sacrificing consciousness to attain something beyond it.

blocks.text: It’s consciousness recognising its own nature.
blocks.directed: It’s consciousness recognising its own nature.

blocks.text: And the external rites become meaningful insofar as they support that recognition.
blocks.directed: And the external rites become meaningful insofar as they support that recognition.

blocks.text: Now, think back to the beginning of the book.
blocks.directed: Now, think back to the beginning of the book.

blocks.text: Knowledge is the cause of liberation.
blocks.directed: Knowledge is the cause of liberation.

blocks.text: And what was the ignorance that had to be overcome?
blocks.directed: And what was the ignorance that had to be overcome?

blocks.text: The contracted apprehension through which consciousness seemed limited.
blocks.directed: The contracted apprehension through which consciousness seemed limited.

blocks.text: And now the whole thing has returned to exactly that problem.
blocks.directed: And now the whole thing has returned to exactly that problem.

blocks.text: The guru appears to possess some power that the disciple lacks.
blocks.directed: The guru appears to possess some power that the disciple lacks.

blocks.text: The rituals appear to be complicated external mechanisms for acquiring something new.
blocks.directed: The rituals appear to be complicated external mechanisms for acquiring something new.

blocks.text: But through the course of the teaching, Abhinavagupta has progressively undermined those assumptions.
blocks.directed: But through the course of the teaching, Abhinavagupta has progressively undermined those assumptions.

blocks.text: The individual is a manifestation of Śiva.
blocks.directed: The individual is a manifestation of Śiva.

blocks.text: The world is a manifestation of Śiva.
blocks.directed: The world is a manifestation of Śiva.

blocks.text: The deity is a manifestation of Śiva.
blocks.directed: The deity is a manifestation of Śiva.

blocks.text: The guru’s liberating power is attributed to Śiva.
blocks.directed: The guru’s liberating power is attributed to Śiva.

blocks.text: And the awareness through which all of these are apprehended?
blocks.directed: And the awareness through which all of these are apprehended?

blocks.text: So the ultimate problem wasn’t that the Supreme Lord had disappeared.
blocks.directed: So the ultimate problem wasn’t that the Supreme Lord had disappeared.

blocks.text: Or that consciousness lacked some foreign property.
blocks.directed: Or that consciousness lacked some foreign property.

blocks.text: Or that the universe had somehow escaped beyond divine freedom.
blocks.directed: Or that the universe had somehow escaped beyond divine freedom.

blocks.text: The problem was the limited apprehension of what was already present.
blocks.directed: The problem was the limited apprehension of what was already present.

blocks.text: And the whole Tantrasāra has been a progressive clarification of that recognition.
blocks.directed: And the whole Tantrasāra has been a progressive clarification of that recognition.
[short pause] Abhinavagupta doesn’t end by saying:

blocks.text: He concludes with a ritual tradition in which all of these become possible supports for recognition.
blocks.directed: He concludes with a ritual tradition in which all of these become possible supports for recognition.
[short pause] But neither does he conclude:

blocks.text: “Do whatever you like and call it Śiva.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Do whatever you like and call it Śiva.”

blocks.text: He has spent whole chapters distinguishing qualification, knowledge, appropriate conduct, initiation and the actual purpose of worship.
blocks.directed: He has spent whole chapters distinguishing qualification, knowledge, appropriate conduct, initiation and the actual purpose of worship.

blocks.text: The recognition of nonduality is not the same thing as indiscriminate indulgence.
blocks.directed: The recognition of nonduality is not the same thing as indiscriminate indulgence.

blocks.text: And that distinction is absolutely essential.
blocks.directed: And that distinction is absolutely essential.

blocks.text: Because the Kaula path is not simply a theology of pleasure.
blocks.directed: Because the Kaula path is not simply a theology of pleasure.

blocks.text: It’s a theology of conscious freedom.
blocks.directed: It’s a theology of conscious freedom.

blocks.text: And all of these are expressions of the one consciousness whose nature is unrestricted.
blocks.directed: And all of these are expressions of the one consciousness whose nature is unrestricted.

blocks.text: Now, what does that mean for liberation?
blocks.directed: Now, what does that mean for liberation?

blocks.text: Not merely the promise of attaining some other place after death.
blocks.directed: Not merely the promise of attaining some other place after death.

blocks.text: But the recognition of the divine reality throughout embodied existence.
blocks.directed: But the recognition of the divine reality throughout embodied existence.

blocks.text: Not that you have to spend your whole life performing increasingly elaborate rituals.
blocks.directed: Not that you have to spend your whole life performing increasingly elaborate rituals.

blocks.text: But that the ultimate nature of the ritual can be recognised within the very awareness through which life is experienced.
blocks.directed: But that the ultimate nature of the ritual can be recognised within the very awareness through which life is experienced.

blocks.text: And then, after all those chapters, Abhinavagupta adds the seventh sacrifice.
blocks.directed: And then, after all those chapters, Abhinavagupta adds the seventh sacrifice.

blocks.text: The living embodiment of the transmission.
blocks.directed: The living embodiment of the transmission.

blocks.text: The recognition communicated through a qualified teacher.
blocks.directed: The recognition communicated through a qualified teacher.

blocks.text: Now imagine the disciple closing the book.
blocks.directed: Now imagine the disciple closing the book.

blocks.text: The most beautiful conceptions of divine consciousness.
blocks.directed: The most beautiful conceptions of divine consciousness.

blocks.text: And the disciple turns to Abhinavagupta.
blocks.directed: And the disciple turns to Abhinavagupta.

blocks.text: And Abhinavagupta gives a little smile.
blocks.directed: And Abhinavagupta gives a little smile.

blocks.text: “You were never ultimately separate from the reality you’ve been studying.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “You were never ultimately separate from the reality you’ve been studying.”

blocks.text: “So what was all this bloody business about?”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “So what was all this bloody business about?”

blocks.text: “The sacred baths, the tridents, the Kālīs, the festivals, the divine couple and the entire Kaula ritual?”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “The sacred baths, the tridents, the Kālīs, the festivals, the divine couple and the entire Kaula ritual?”

blocks.text: The recognition of one’s own essential nature.
blocks.directed: The recognition of one’s own essential nature.

blocks.text: You thought you were a little individual reading an enormous book to discover the nature of Śiva.
blocks.directed: You thought you were a little individual reading an enormous book to discover the nature of Śiva.

blocks.text: And Abhinavagupta has spent the entire book explaining that the reality through which the reading, the understanding, the doubt and the recognition occur is itself the supreme consciousness.
blocks.directed: And Abhinavagupta has spent the entire book explaining that the reality through which the reading, the understanding, the doubt and the recognition occur is itself the supreme consciousness.

blocks.text: So, after all this time, who’s reading?
blocks.directed: So, after all this time, who’s reading?

blocks.text: The whole bloody business is Śiva.
blocks.directed: The whole bloody business is Śiva.
